---
title: "Processor migration to Cloudflare"
description: "Per-job plan and cost bounds for moving scheduled processors off Vercel, with checkout expiry as the Worker template."
updatedAt: '2026-10-23'
audience: developers
---

Moving a job's **schedule** into Cron Control
still invokes its Vercel function every slot. Moving its **processor** into a
Worker, Queue consumer or Workflow removes that invocation. Follow
Cloudflare backend ownership and the
[runaway-work acceptance](/build/development-tools/oxc-cloudflare-adoption#runaway-work-and-cost-acceptance)
rules for every move.

## Template: checkout expiry Worker processor

`apps/cron-control/src/processors/checkout-expiry.ts` ports Inventory's
checkout-expiry processor. It runs only when `inventory-checkout-expiry` is in
both `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` and `CRON_CONTROL_WORKER_PROCESSORS`, so the
schedule and processor can be selected independently. The Inventory job is
absent from both selectors in source.

- **Same claim.** The Worker calls the private `expire_inventory_checkout_sessions`
  RPC directly with the service key in `apikey`. The RPC locks candidates with
  `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and only moves `reserved` rows, so a concurrent legacy
  run cannot double-expire a checkout.
- **Expiry bounds and backpressure.** At most 10 batches of 1,000 rows per slot,
  one shared `p_now`, 30-second database deadlines and manual redirects. Check the
  durable stop fence before every batch and revalidation chunk. Active obligations
  and quarantined work share a 5,000-workspace bound. Reserve room for a worst-case
  1,000 distinct workspaces before each expiry RPC; stop expiry when capacity is
  insufficient. Ledger overflow is refused atomically; no oldest-item eviction.
- **Whole-run deadline.** Claim, HTTP headers/body, pending-ledger RPCs, stop checks
  and completion share an absolute 240-second deadline inside the 270-second lease.
  HTTP requests also retain their shorter timeout. A timed-out ledger call can
  still complete remotely; do not replay it immediately. No dependent operation
  starts after timeout. Late obligation settlement and retry charges are fenced
  by the original claim's generation and slot. An unconfirmed completion leaves the claim to be charged
  as unknown by the next slot rather than reporting success.
- **Owed work first.** Outstanding revalidation runs before any expiry, with up to
  120 seconds reserved for that phase. If owed work remains, start no new
  expiry. Fresh expiries persist obligations before revalidation. Incomplete work,
  capacity exhaustion and quarantine never count as a successful slot.
- **Per-workspace receipts.** Next.js owns storefront cache invalidation. The Worker
  posts at most 100 workspace UUIDs to Inventory's authenticated POST adapter
  (8 KiB input bound). The adapter uses the throwing invalidation helper, isolates
  each workspace failure and returns `results: [{ wsId, ok }]`. Only an explicit
  `ok: true` receipt for a requested workspace settles its obligation. Missing,
  contradictory, failed or legacy aggregate-only receipts stay owed.
- **Poison isolation.** A failed chunk does not prevent later chunks from running
  within the remaining time. Each unconfirmed item gets one durable attempt charge
  per sweep. After three attempts it moves to bounded `quarantinedWork`; the item
  is retained, occupies capacity and is not retried automatically. Healthy chunks
  can still settle. Inspect quarantine through the authenticated ledger status;
  repair and confirm invalidation before deliberately settling it. Resume alone
  preserves quarantine. Five failed or unknown slots still stop the entire job.

**Operation envelope.** An idle Worker slot makes five ledger calls (claim, two
backlog reads, stop check, completion) and one expiry RPC, with no Inventory call.
A slot makes at most 10 expiry RPCs and 100 revalidation calls (50 owed chunks plus
50 fresh chunks), with at most three ledger operations per revalidation chunk
(fence, settle, failure charge). These are conservative source bounds, not billed
usage or hosted acceptance. Quarantined items have no automatic retries; stopped
jobs do no processor work. The controlled unit fixtures count requests and cover
capacity, partial receipts, poison isolation, restart persistence and each stalled
ledger phase. Hosted stop, database, Next cache freshness and exact-artifact CI
remain separate gates. Database expiry and recording a ledger obligation are
separate writes; an interruption between them still requires reconciliation
before claiming crash-atomic end-to-end invalidation.

**Cutover.** Verify the per-workspace receipt adapter and Worker processor before
the production handoff. The Inventory job is absent from both selectors in
source. Disable and drain the Vercel schedule before selecting the job and its
Worker processor in production. Verify `detail.expired`, storefront freshness,
and the durable stop before the Inventory route cutover. Follow the
[Inventory scheduler handoff and rollback](/build/devops/inventory-start-void#move-checkout-expiry-to-cron-control).

Regression coverage: `src/processors/checkout-expiry.test.ts` counts RPC and
revalidation calls for idle, draining, capped, stopped, partially failed, deadline,
malformed and chunked cases; `src/dispatch.test.ts` proves the port runs only when
selected; the Inventory route test covers revalidation auth and input bounds.

## Native maintenance: external-app exchange audit retention

`external-app-exchange-audit-retention` deletes `private.external_app_exchange_events`
rows older than 180 days, measured by the database clock, through
`private.purge_external_app_exchange_events(p_limit)`. Migration
`20261123024500_external_app_exchange_events.sql`, which lands separately from
the job, creates that function: `security definer`, executable only by
`service_role`, returning the deleted count as an integer, with no `pg_cron`
schedule. The job runs daily at 02:43 GMT+7 (`43 19 * * *`), sharing
the AI Studio retention trigger, so it adds no Worker invocation. Like every Cron
Control job, it stays off until `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` names it.

Bounds per daily slot:

| Operation | At most |
| --- | --- |
| Purge RPC calls (`p_limit` 1,000) | 8, ending at the first page below 1,000 |
| Rows deleted | 8,000 |
| Ledger operations | claim, one fence check before each call (8), outcome record |
| In-slot retries | 0 |

An empty table costs one call. Eight full pages, or a deadline that leaves less
than 40 seconds (one call's 30-second timeout plus the outcome write), end the
slot as `degraded` with
`detail.capped`; the remaining backlog waits for the next daily slot. A closed
fence ends the slot as `stopped` before the next call. A 4xx is `failed`; a 5xx,
a network error or an invalid count is `unknown`, because rows may have been
deleted. Outcomes charge the shared failure budget, except a `PGRST202` 404
before the grace date, so five consecutive charged slots stop the job.

Until `RPC_MISSING_GRACE_UNTIL` (2026-12-07 23:59 GMT+7), a 404 whose capped
(1 KiB) body carries PostgREST's `PGRST202` means the migration has not applied
yet. The processor then logs `EXTERNAL_APP_EXCHANGE_AUDIT_RPC_MISSING`, makes no
further call and records `stopped` with `detail.rpcMissing`: one call a day.
After that date, or without `PGRST202`, a 404 is `failed`.

Expected volume is about one row per external-app sign-in (code exchange) or
token refresh. More than 8,000 new rows a day would outgrow the daily slot: the
backlog would keep growing while the job reports only `degraded`, so watch
`detail.capped` before admitting it.

Regression coverage: `apps/cron-control/src/external-app-exchange-audit-retention.test.ts`
counts calls for the default-off, empty, full-then-short, eight-full-page,
deadline-pressure, fence-closed, missing-function before and after the grace
date, non-`PGRST202` 404, 5xx failure-budget and invalid-count cases.

## Per-job plan

| Job | Processor target | Work bounds to keep | Cost change when moved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inventory-checkout-expiry` | Worker processor (implemented, off) | 10 × 1,000 rows, revalidation chunks of 100 | −288 Vercel invocations a day |
| `tasks-cleanup-media` | Worker processor with a durable workspace cursor in the ledger | Page storage listings, bound workspaces per slot, keep the 30-day retention and reference checks | −1 long (300 s) invocation a day; deletes stay idempotent |
| `pay-products` | Worker processor | Page Polar products at 100, keep upsert by provider id | −2 a day |
| `infrastructure-sync-trust-cache` | Worker processor writing the trust cache over REST | Keep 32-way write concurrency and the 2-hour TTL | −144 a day |
| `calendar-provider-sync` | Queue consumer, one message per workspace | Keep the per-workspace cooldown; align Queue retries with it | −96 gateway invocations a day; adds Queue operations per workspace |
| `calendar-smart-schedule` | Workflow per workspace | Persist step results; finite attempts | −4 a day |
| `web-notification-batches`, `web-post-email-queue`, `web-topic-announcements`, `web-report-automation` | Queue consumers | Keep the existing row claims and send reconciliation; one attempt budget across Queue and claims | −336 a day; adds Queue operations per batch |
| `web-deadline-reminders` | Worker processor after the receipt check becomes an atomic claim | Make check-and-record one RPC before porting | −288 a day |
| `finance-exchange-rates` | Worker processor | One provider call a day | −1 a day |
| `infrastructure-sample-resources`, `infrastructure-docker-recovery-alerts` | Retire, pending owner decision | They read the retired Docker host | −1,728 a day if retired |

Ports that need Next.js-only effects (cache tags, React email rendering) keep a
small authenticated adapter in the owning app, called only when work happened,
until that app itself moves to Cloudflare. Durable business work never relies on
`ctx.waitUntil`.
